title: Insurance Claim (Third-Party Billing): Non-Covered Write-Off of Self-Administered Drugs on Observation and Emergency Claims
content:
**Denials desk note.** On a Commercial PPO, Commercial HMO or Marketplace claim in denied status for an Observation Stay Account or an Emergency Department Visit Account, this rule takes the self-administered drugs off the claim as one write-off entry with the write-off reason NONCOVERED_NO_WAIVER, carrying the claim's current denial reason code; any other claim gets nothing here.

The self-administered drugs are billed on the Observation Stay Account or Emergency Department Visit Account of the patient's Hospital Account (Encounter Billing); the claim is the Insurance Claim (Third-Party Billing) for that account.

**What the write-off amount replaces.** For the self-administered drugs of a claim closed under this rule, and only for them, the amount written off as non-covered with no waiver is the self-administered drug value rather than their charges; small items on Riverbend's outpatient-surgery small-item list, take-home convenience items, the services closed on the member's decision, small items on Riverbend's observation and emergency small-item list and the services closed on the patient's external-review decision are written off under their own rules, and every other denied amount is written off in full by the hospital, never billed to the patient, when its route ends in a write-off: timely filing expired (no timely-filing proof), no authorization obtained (no authorization, notification, emergency exemption or retro authorization), non-covered with no waiver (no advance waiver on file), appeals exhausted (the last available level upheld the denial), or below the appeal threshold (a denied amount at or below the payer class's small-denial write-off amount that is not worth appealing).

**What stays on the claim.** The self-administered drug charges above that value stay on the claim as the contractual remainder, which Riverbend's month-end contractual close posts on the last calendar day of the month.

## Booking the write-off: `write_off_self_administered_drugs_664aab61`
**Capability.** Writes off, on one insurance claim, the value of self-administered drugs that no payer covers on an outpatient claim and for which no advance financial-responsibility waiver is on file: one write-off entry with the write-off reason NONCOVERED_NO_WAIVER and the claim's current denial reason code, dated today, lowering the amount still expected from the payer on that claim by the same figure. The patient is never billed for it; the claim's status does not change.

**Invocation.** An agent-side tool: the agent unlocks `write_off_self_administered_drugs_664aab61` and then calls it.

**Parameters**
| Parameter | Meaning and format |
|---|---|
| `claim_id` | the reference number of the insurance claim whose self-administered drugs are written off, as shown by the claim lookup for the patient |
| `amount_usd` | the self-administered drug value being written off: USD, 2 decimal places, positive magnitude, already rounded to the cent by the caller; posted exactly as given |

**Return.** A text receipt: "Write-off <entry_id> posted on claim <claim_id>: <amount_usd> USD, reason NONCOVERED_NO_WAIVER, denial code <carc_code>; amount still expected from the payer <payer_balance> USD." The denial code is the claim's denial reason code copied onto the entry; the payer balance is the new amount still expected from the payer (USD, 2 decimal places). The receipt appearing is the success signal.
